At this point I more or less accepted the fact that Windows is going to spy on me no matter what I do. Even if people on the internet think they disabled it all, it's pretty difficult to prove without a doubt that Windows is no longer spying on you. The best thing you can do is install Linux or BSD on your computer and dual boot, and only use Windows as little as possible. A lot of what you do on the computer now is done through a browser. I think that you won't feel like you're missing much, and to be honest, Linux has some great programs and you can run some Windows programs in Linux through WINE. You can also us a Windows virtual machine in Linux, which works great for anything besides games (though you can use it for games if you use a VM passthrough).

I only really use Windows for watching TV shows and playing games. I spend the vast majority of time in Linux. I think it's about the only way. I realize not every line of Linux and a desktop environment has been security audited, but at least it is capable of being audited. Windows can do whatever it wants and obfuscate things from reverse engineering and no one will ever know.
